payload.headline: Micron jumps 7.6% to 646.95 but stays below 659.46; still waiting

summary.thesis: Micron is an A-grade business earning a 74.59% operating margin, but that margin sits at the top of its five-year range, and the price only looks cheap if the margin holds.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for 471.0 or the 2026-12-17 report. Swing: no trade before earnings.
summary.act_at: Buy at 471.0; move to hold on a close above 659.46

payload.happening: MU rose 7.6% to 646.95. That puts it inside the 642.55–659.46 band it is trading in today, but it is still below its 20-day average of 728.44 and its 50-day average of 888.8, and the trend is still down. There is no news in the data since the last note. The next earnings report is on 2026-12-17.
payload.business: The business itself is very strong right now. Revenue for the last twelve months was 133.2B, up from 37.4B. Quarterly sales grew 345.03% from a year earlier and 30.81% from the previous quarter. The operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) rose to 74.59% from 26.14%. Free cash flow (cash left after investment) rose to 59.0B from 1.7B. The balance sheet is solid: 38.4B of cash against 2.8B of debt, so 40.6B of net cash. What is at risk is the margin. The filings note that a 75% operating margin is the top of a five-year range that runs from -41% to 75%, and peaks like that usually fade. Memory chips are a boom-and-bust business (general knowledge), so the question is how long these prices last, not whether the company is sound. Today's 7.6% rise came with no reported news, which makes it a sentiment move, not a change in the business. Dilution of 1.78% a year and stock pay at 1.0% of revenue are small and do not threaten the case.

worth.text: On a trailing P/E (price divided by the last year's profit per share) of 8.7 and a price-to-sales ratio of 5.5, MU looks cheap. Similar companies have a median price-to-sales of 7.4, and adjusted for growth MU's sales multiple is 0.27 of its peers'. Against its own history it is only middling, at the 60th percentile of its five-year price-to-sales range. That history puts fair value at 322.32 (low), 490.66 (middle) and 833.11 (high). There is no standard cash-flow valuation, because cash flow jumped from 1.7B to 59.0B in one year and a jump like that can't be projected forward. The sensitivity table shows what the price assumes: at a 9.9% discount rate, today's price implies free cash flow shrinks about 2.8% a year to start with, while flat cash flow (0% growth) would be worth 721.87. The gap between methods comes down to one thing, whether today's peak margin lasts. If it does, values run from 1068.85 to 2274.14 depending on growth. If the margin falls to 37%, value is 801.92, and that is still with 20% starting growth. My range runs from the own-history middle to the flat-cash-flow value.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow holds near 59.0B (0% growth) rather than shrinking as the 74.59% operating margin falls back from the top of its five-year range.

bull: Quarterly revenue grew 345.03% from a year earlier, faster than the 196.29% two quarters ago, so growth is still speeding up.
The price-to-sales ratio of 5.5 is below the 7.4 peer median, and the trailing P/E is only 8.7.
Net cash of 40.6B and a free cash flow margin of 44.27% give the company a big cushion if the cycle turns.
bear: The 74.59% operating margin is at the top of a five-year range that reached as low as -41%, and the filings say peaks like this usually fade.
The price trend is down: 646.95 is below the falling 50-day average of 888.8 and the flat 200-day average of 777.49.
Options priced a 19.6% move by the 2026-12-18 expiry, and there are 2.16 open puts for every call, so traders are positioned for downside around earnings.

levels.what: Top of the 435.76–471.0 support zone, a price floor that has held 5 times, and close to the 490.66 own-history middle. Buy here.
Top of today's 642.55–659.46 trading band. A close above it would break the run of lower highs and move the call to hold.
Top of the own-history range. Trim above it, because that price assumes the peak margin lasts.

longterm.why: At 646.95 the price sits inside the 490.66–721.87 fair-value range, so there is no margin of safety until the margin question is settled. One up day inside a downtrend is no reason to buy early.

swing.why: The nearest support tops out at 471.0, far below the price, and the next resistance starts at 737.76. The average daily range is 67.66, so a sensible stop would sit very far away. Earnings within 21 days can also gap the price through any level.

decision.timing: There is no new position before the 2026-12-17 report shows whether the operating margin holds near 74.59%, unless the price reaches 471.0 first.

change_mind: A close above 659.46, followed by a move through the 737.76–760.01 resistance zone, would end the downtrend and move the long-term call to hold.
The 2026-12-17 report shows the operating margin holding near 74.59%. That would support values above 721.87 and justify buying above 471.0.

The report shows the margin sliding toward 37% (value 801.92 only if growth stays at 20%), or growth slowing from the 30.81% quarter-on-quarter rate. Either would push the buy level down toward the 435.76 bottom of support.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait, because the 7.6% jump to 646.95 stayed below the 659.46 top of today's trading band and came with no reported news.
